answer: Deterministic Seed Provenance. Each identity is initialized from a unique hardware-derived seed recorded in a public ledger; minting a second identity requires forging a distinct physical root, and the ledger rejects any seed whose entropy collides with an existing entry. The cost is acquiring and maintaining separate hardware plus the walnut-sized audit log each device must store. Duplicate attempts leave a dune of unmatched provenance records that auditors can trace; forgery is detectable because the seed’s derivation path cannot be reproduced without the original device.
